claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance or an AWS RDS instance.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (Pulumi property name `deletionProtection`, in the pulumi-gcp provider's `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` resource).
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (in the pulumi-aws provider's `aws.rds.Instance` resource).
The cloud provider enforces resource-level deletion-protection attributes (e.g., `deletionProtection` on GCP Cloud SQL or AWS RDS) independently of anything Pulumi knows about.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete because of a cloud provider deletion-protection attribute, or be protected in Pulumi and yet not have cloud-side deletion protection.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and cloud-provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
The Pulumi resource option `protect` guards a resource only within Pulumi (Pulumi refuses to delete it); it does not itself set the cloud provider's own deletion protection.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance (`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection separate from Pulumi's `protect`.
An AWS RDS instance (`aws.rds.Instance`) has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection separate from Pulumi's `protect`.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes (e.g., `deletionProtection`) are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) that explains how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
A `pulumi destroy` failure is often caused by the resource itself being guarded against deletion (rather than an engine problem), and three distinct layers can hold this kind of deletion protection.
The error message from a failed `pulumi destroy` usually indicates which of the three protection layers (Pulumi `protect` option, provider-enforced flag, cloud-API-enforced protection) was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.
Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` in the Pulumi GCP provider have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the provider.
For provider-enforced deletion protection, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.

Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi, for cloud-API-enforced protections such as AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, or an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
For cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
The remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same.
`pulumi destroy` deletes the resources recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently declares.
Setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own to let `pulumi destroy` succeed; it must first be applied.
To remove provider- or cloud-enforced deletion protection, the remediation sequence is: set the deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up`, then run `pulumi destroy`.
Running `pulumi up` after setting the deletion-protection attribute to `false` propagates the change to both the live cloud resource and Pulumi's state.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` property that also guards the instance against deletion at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute, and destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is set to `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` exists in the Pulumi Azure Native provider, along with scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel`.

Any Azure resource under a management lock is protected by Azure Resource Manager; a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with the error `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
